I have Scrooge McDuck - Ghostly Ebenezer with 3 cards under him.. Oponnent plays Hades - Looking for a deal, and I choose to hide Scrooge under deck..

Hey Alain, I know this is a very old post but I'm looking to learn more about this ruling. 

What is the difference with Syndrome's Remote being able to trigger and banish this item and discarding to draw.

respuestas.autor_original: Jacob Smith [LRH], Etiqueta de servidor: LRHLRHLore Guide
respuestas.texto:
There are two different types of abilities at play here. 

LEARN FROM THEIR LOSSES is a triggered ability. When its condition is met ("whenever a robot character is banished") its effect is put into the bag. ("You may banish this item to draw two cards.") When the bag is next resolved, you take the effect out and resolve it. 

MISSING PIECE is a static ability that is always applying. If a Buzz was banished, it gives an alternate method for playing Buzz's Arm. It doesn't ever resolve or get played, it just is always checking and giving you that option when it's appropriate. 
In order to take advantage of that alternate cost, you still need to be able to play the item, which you usually only have the ability to do during your own main phase. (editado)lunes, 15 de junio de 2026, 14:

Takeback Policy Question:

Alice is sitting at 11 lore and sees they can quest for 9 to win the game.  Because their opponent currently has 13 Lore.

They in a single "batch" action start exerting their characters from left to right exerting Milo, then Milo, then The Queen while saying

preguntas.autor_original: Danxor [LRH], Etiqueta de servidor: LRHLRHCommunity Collaborator
preguntas.texto: Rewind of all the questing? Or just the Queen as that was the only spot something diverged on what they said and what happened?

I thought the policy directly applied to batching things that can't be batched, like questing, and being lenient to how players typically play.

I can see the application of GRE though, that makes sense otherwise

respuestas.texto: take back seems okay here?

I think this is the exact kind of “gotcha” the policy was written to discourage, but it doesn’t strictly apply. The player clearly knows how The Queen’s ability works, because otherwise they wouldn’t see that they have game on board.

However, because the order of questing affects the outcome of the action, they cannot be executed in an OoOS - that policy doesn’t apply. Thus they cannot be taken back as a single batched action, because they can’t be a single batched action.

On the other, other hand, that makes attempting to batch them together a GRE. A warning and rewind would be appropriate.
The full sequence. The error is batching all the quests together.
(IMO)

respuestas.autor_original: Ellie [LRH], Etiqueta de servidor: LRHLRHCommunity Collaborator
respuestas.texto: Since they incorrectly resolved the ability, that's a GRE... they didn't miss it. I'm inclined to rewind the batch.

The OoOS policy allows players to batch things that the game rules do not allow to be batched - by the CRD alone, nothing can be batched because that’s not how the game works.

However, to legally batch things under the OoOS exception, the order in which the actions being batched are carried out must make no difference to the resolution of the sequence. In this case, that’s not true, because the order of questing will change the lore value gained - so it cannot be a legally batched sequence.

If the batched action is not legal, then it can’t really be considered a “batched action” for the take back policy, and is instead a game error.

(Although ultimately whether or not to allow a take back here doesn’t actually matter, because there was still a GRE either way so the rewind will do the same thing as a take back would and they would still receive the corrective action whether a take back was allowed or not).

For Chris:
OoOS - Out of Order Sequencing (policy in the tournament rules)
CRD - comprehensive rules document

Okay.  I can only speak for how I would have handled this at a Set Championship I was running, because I would opt to deviate from competitive play correction here to use it as a learning experience for a young player.  I am sure there are other judges who would rule differently.

If I were HJ at this event, and you approached me with the issue, I would want to sit down with you both and clear up which cards are there vs which ones are reported. Without knowing full context and having full investigation information, at a set champs I was running, I would let her continue to play the deck she brought but assess a formal warning. That's technically the corrective action described in the PCG for cases where the decklist has to be altered so you can't blame the Lore Guide for applying the "correct" correction.

However if I were HJ at said set champ I would also consider everything in the context, one of them being the fact that Set Championships are supposed to be uniformly run across all stores, yet most of them (at least in my area) don't collect decklists even though they are required to do so.
Had the same error happened in a store that did not care about decklists, it would have never been detected and never considered an error.

Contrary to kleptokatt I would have still issued a Warning for DRE Minor instead of a Caution if she could find the cards to match the submitted decklist. The reason is that upgrading 2 Warning to a Game Loss in DRE Minor is never supposed to happen, the player had a deck not matching the decklist, during the first DRE we changed the cards to match the decklist and unless the player intentionally changes cards back, the same error is not supposed to happen again in the tournament.
And the Warning is important to track that it's the second time it happened in case it actually does, which would get to an investigation to check that she is not siding her deck depending on matchups. 

If she could not find the cards however, I would apply the remedy and alter the decklist to match the deck if the deck is indeed legal but also issue a GRE Major Warning instead of the prescribed GL given context and how she was "victim" of the store running the event correctly by actually collecting the decklists.

If this happened again in the tournament this Warning would however also be upgraded to a GL.

1.9.5. If a character or effect would deal damage and that damage is reduced to 0 when modifiers are applied, the character or effect is still considered to “deal” damage. preguntas.texto:
Seeking clarification on the new rule changes for damage.

If my character receives [ACT OF KINDESS] from my [Rapunzel - Ready for Adventure], what happens when opponent challenges it with a character with 0 strength?

Since the opposing character would literally under new terms “deal 0 damage”, and then “dealt 0 damage” to my character. Would the replacement effect of [ACT OF KINDNESS] be consumed? Since it just reads “the next time they would be dealt damage”. I would assume “dealt 0 damage” still causes it to be consumed since 0 is a valid damage.

Hmm, still kinda weird, what if the opposing character had 1 strength, but is applied an effect of -1 strength (lets say by Rhino - One-Sixteenth Wolf). 

Since the damage is now modified, 1.9.5 will apply. Does this mean the eventual “dealt 0 damage” during Damage Calculation step will consume Rapunzel’s shield?

respuestas.texto:
1.9.5. If a character or effect would deal damage and that damage is reduced to 0 when modifiers are applied, the character or effect is still considered to “deal” damage.

If the character has a strength of 0 or less, then the character wouldn't deal damage in the first place, so 1.9.5 doesn't apply.

I would have thought that 1.9.5 was for things like resist, where there was damage but it was negated. The rhino example above would (in my mind) deal no damage because they had 0 strength and therefore there was no damage in the first place. I'm likely wrong though!

Even with the addition of 1.9.5, 5.3.6.2 still applies:

5.3.6.2. Strength  – Primarily, how much damage this character deals in a challenge, though card effects can also reference this value. If a character would deal damage equal to its  and it has 0 or less , it deals no damage.

contexto.texto:
In my mind, I’m just thinking, since now everything is “Deal” -> “Dealt” -> “Take”.

And Rapunzel did not specifically state “the next time they would be dealt more than 1 damage”…in this case would a “dealt 0 damage” event consume the shield since “dealt 0 damage” is, to me, still considered “the next time they would be dealt damage”.

Under 4.6.6.1 “First, calculate the total amount of damage dealt to each character in the challenge. If a character’s strength is negative, it counts as 0 strength for the purpose of determining how much damage is dealt during the challenge.”

It does not explicitly state that if the character strength is 0, the “dealt 0 damage” event does not occur at all in 4.6.6.2.
Ah great, ty. I was zoomed in on the challenge clauses and missed this. So indeed there is a clause which is 5.3.6.2 to explicitly state that 0 strength means deal no damage.
Guess there will be no 0 damage shenanigans to remove Rapunzel’s shield.
